title: Diagnostics manifest v1
description: The single serialization a quantisation-error diagnostic run emits. The Markdown report (REP-002), the daemon routes (API-012) and the heat-map surface all derive from this document; a number that appears in one of them and not here is a bug. Implemented by `q_report::Manifest` (crates/q-report/src/manifest.rs); this schema and those types must agree, and crates/q-report/tests/schema_conformance.rs fails if they drift. Shape follows .plan/REPORT_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.

manifest_version.description: Version of this document format. A reader refuses a version it does not know rather than guessing a layout, the same rule CAT-002 applies to the catalog schema; a breaking change mints /v2 and both may exist during migration (SCHEMA_PLAN.md section 5).

projection.description: Which projection of the run this document is. Required rather than inferred from whether `tensors` is present, because `full` with an empty `tensors` (nothing was examined, and `refusals` says why) and `summary` (the per-tensor array was deliberately left out) are different facts, and a consumer that cannot tell them apart will report one as the other.

run.description: What ran, on what backend, and what it cost.

model.description: Which checkpoint was diagnosed. A diagnosis of an unidentified checkpoint is not evidence, so every identity field here is required and non-empty.

config.description: The quantisation configuration that was simulated. v1 computes the quantised counterpart itself and never reads a third-party quantised artifact (DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md section 1).

layers.description: Per layer of the repeated stack, ordered by `layer_index`. `layer_index` is unique within the array.

experts.description: Per MoE expert, ordered by (`layer_index`, `expert_index`). Empty where the resolver found no experts — absence here means the model has none or the resolver did not recognise them, never that expert error was zero.

tensors.description: Per examined tensor, ordered by canonical address. Present exactly when `projection` is `full`. At CAT-006's 47278 tensors this array is tens of megabytes, which is acceptable on disk and is not acceptable to push into a browser wholesale (ARCHITECTURE.md section 19); that is what the `summary` projection exists for.

ranking.description: Tensors ranked by relative weight-space error, a proxy for sensitivity — not a statement that a layer is important, which is task-relative and not measured here. Ordered by (relative_error descending, parameter_count descending, address ascending), a total order because addresses are unique. Every address also appears in `tensors` when the projection is `full`.

frontier.description: The mixed-precision frontier: which tensors to keep at base precision, and what that costs in bytes.

fidelity.description: How the numbers in this manifest were obtained. The same three-way vocabulary the data model types end to end (SRC-018, STAT-005); a sampled result must never be presented as an exact one.

refusals.description: Every capability this run could not provide, each with its requirement ID, ordered by (requirement_id, what, why). Required and never omitted: a consumer must be able to tell 'zero' from 'not computed', which is the failure mode that destroys trust in a diagnostic tool. An empty array is a claim that nothing was refused.

run_id.description: Deterministic identifier derived from (model revision hash, config, engine version). Two runs over the same inputs share it, which is what makes a cached or repeated run recognisable as the same run.

engine_version.description: Version of the diagnostics engine that produced this document. Part of the determinism contract: same checkpoint plus same config plus same engine version gives byte-identical output.

backend.description: Which compute backend actually ran. `cpu` is the numerical ground truth; `metal` is an accelerator behind the same trait. There is deliberately no `cuda`: q-cuda is Hardware-Unverified (CUDA-001), and claiming a GPU computed something the CPU computed is on the forbidden-claims list (PRODUCT_SCOPE.md section 5.2). A vocabulary that can name a backend which has never run is how that claim gets made by accident.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. `2026-08-04T00:00:00Z`. Wall-clock metadata: excluded from the determinism comparison, so that a diff of two configs shows the numbers that changed and not the clock (REPORT_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.2).

elapsed_seconds.description: Wall-clock duration. Run metadata, excluded from the determinism comparison for the same reason as `started_at`.

peak_resident_bytes.description: Measured peak resident set size for the run, in bytes. The product's central claim — bounded residency independent of checkpoint size — lives here, in the artifact, so a reader never has to take it on trust. Must be above zero: a performance number does not exist until it is measured, and a run that could not measure residency records a refusal rather than reporting nothing as zero.

bytes_read.description: Total payload bytes read from the checkpoint. Two passes over a tensor are expected where the granularity needs a whole-axis view (DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md section 5).

source_uri.description: Where the checkpoint was read from.

revision_hash.description: Revision of the checkpoint as its source names it. Required and non-empty: a diagnosis that cannot say which checkpoint it diagnosed is not evidence, and a report of it must be refused rather than emitted.

checkpoint_bytes.description: Size of the checkpoint on disk.

parameter_count.description: Total parameters in the checkpoint. May exceed the sum over `tensors` when a tensor was refused — see `refusals`.

architecture.description: The architecture plugin that produced the hierarchy — one of the resolvers under `architectures/`, e.g. `llama`, `qwen`, `generic`. Not an enum, so that adding a plugin does not require a schema version bump.

resolver_confidence.description: `resolved` when an architecture plugin recognised the hierarchy, `unknown` when the generic resolver produced it. Surfaced because a generic-resolved model has weaker layer semantics, and NSIR-001 forbids presenting a guessed hierarchy as a known one.

kind.description: Which values share one scale. Defined against NSIR's canonical axis semantics rather than raw tensor order: `per_output_channel` means one scale per output channel regardless of how the checkpoint stores the matrix (DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.2).

group_size.description: Values per group. Present exactly when `kind` is `per_group`; the block grid is aligned to it so that group-wise quantisation needs no second pass.

precision.description: Target precision of the simulated quantisation.

granularity.description: Which values share one quantisation scale.

round.description: Rounding mode. `nearest_even` is the only v1 variant, stated explicitly because half-away-from-zero disagrees with NumPy on exactly the boundary values a golden test contains.

block_rows.description: Rows per streamed block. Residency is proportional to the block, not to the tensor.

resident_ceiling_bytes.description: The declared residency ceiling the run was asked to stay under. Compare with `run.peak_resident_bytes`.

error_aggregate.description: The composable partials for one level of the aggregation hierarchy (channel to tensor to module to layer to expert to model). Partials only: sums of squares compose across blocks, RMSE and relative error do not, and computing a finished metric per block and averaging is the single most likely correctness bug in this engine. A consumer derives rmse = sqrt(sum_sq_delta / count) and relative_error = sqrt(sum_sq_delta / sum_sq_base) at read time. Storing the finished metric here as well would give one quantity two definitions, and two definitions drift.

count.description: Number of weights reduced at this level.

sum_sq_base.description: Sum of w squared — the denominator of relative error.

sum_sq_delta.description: Sum of (w - w-hat) squared — the numerator, the squared Frobenius norm of the error before the root.

max_abs_delta.description: Maximum |w - w-hat|. Exact on every backend: a max reduction has no rounding excuse.

bytes_at_base_precision.description: Bytes these weights occupy at the checkpoint's own precision.

bytes_at_target_precision.description: Bytes these weights would occupy at `config.precision`. The difference is what keeping this level at base precision costs.

layer_index.description: Zero-based index within the repeated layer stack.

aggregate.description: Partials summed over every tensor in this layer.

expert_index.description: Expert index within the layer, as NSIR-003 resolves it.

aggregate.description: Partials summed over this expert's tensors. Weight-space redundancy may be read from these numbers; expert deadness may not, because deadness is a routing property that needs runtime.

outlier_attribution.description: Share of squared error carried by the largest weights by magnitude (DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.1). A tensor whose error is mostly attributable to 0.1 percent of its weights is a candidate for an outlier-preserving scheme; a tensor with diffuse error is not. Entirely weight-space.

top_0_1_percent_share.description: Fraction of this tensor's squared error carried by the largest 0.1 percent of its weights by magnitude.

top_1_percent_share.description: Fraction of this tensor's squared error carried by the largest 1 percent of its weights by magnitude.

address.description: NSIR canonical address, e.g. `model.layers[10].self_attention.query_projection.weight` (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.1). Unique across the array (SRC-006).

role.description: Semantic role, in q_source::TensorRole's own spellings. `unknown` is a legitimate value, not a gap: ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.2 forbids guessing a role from shape, and a spelling outside this set is refused rather than coerced to `unknown` — that would make a typo read as an honest admission of ignorance.

dtype.description: SafeTensors dtype tag, in the header spellings q_source::DType defines. A tag outside this set is refused, never guessed (SRC-014).

shape.description: Shape in axis order. Rank is capped at 3: ADR-010 implements rank at most 3 and refuses above it rather than flattening, because a [32,128,128] tensor presented as [32,16384] is a confidently wrong picture that invites the reader to see adjacency between values that are not adjacent. A rank-4 tensor is recorded in `refusals` under GRID-007; it never appears here reshaped.

outlier_attribution.description: Where this tensor's error concentrates. Absent when it was not computed — absence is not a zero, and a run that skipped it records a refusal.

address.description: Canonical address of the ranked tensor.

relative_error.description: sqrt(sum_sq_delta / sum_sq_base) for this tensor. Carried here, and only here, because it is the ordering key; everywhere else the manifest carries partials and the consumer finishes the arithmetic. A proxy for sensitivity, ranked — not an accuracy prediction and not a claim that the tensor matters.

parameter_count.description: Parameters in this tensor. The first tie-break, descending.

keep_set.description: Canonical addresses kept at base precision at this step, ascending and distinct. When the projection is `full` every address also appears in `tensors`.

added_bytes.description: Cumulative bytes the keep set costs, relative to quantising everything to `config.precision`. Computed, not estimated.

error_removed_fraction.description: Cumulative fraction of total squared weight-space error removed by this keep set. Computed exactly from two measured quantities. Not an accuracy prediction: accuracy impact is not measured by this tool.

method.description: How the frontier was searched. Greedy over the density ratio (error removed per byte kept) — the standard fractional-knapsack heuristic.

claim.description: The strength of the claim, fixed so that no consumer can render a frontier without it. The heuristic is not proven optimal for the integer problem, and DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 requires this wording wherever the frontier is presented.
claim.const: Greedy over error-per-byte; not proven optimal.

steps.description: The frontier itself, ordered by cumulative `added_bytes`. Empty when no frontier was computed — and then `refusals` says why.

requirement_id.description: The STATUS.md requirement ID for the declared gap, e.g. `EVAL-001` for accuracy estimation or `GRID-007` for a tensor above the implemented rank ceiling.

what.description: What this run could not provide.

why.description: Why not, in the wording the governing document requires. A refusal that does not say why reads as a bug rather than a boundary.

frontier.claim: Greedy over error-per-byte; not proven optimal.

refusals.why: Weight-space error only. Accuracy impact is not measured — run your evaluation on the recommended configuration.
The run was cancelled before the first tensor completed. Nothing was measured; the zeroes above are the absence of a measurement, not a measurement of zero.
